posts.title: Large pothole causing traffic issues
posts.desc: This pothole has been getting bigger and is causing vehicle damage.
posts.address: 4120 Finch Ave E, near Birchmount Rd
details: A pothole on the eastbound curb lane of Finch Ave E has widened to roughly 70 cm across and about 15 cm deep. It sits directly in the path of traffic merging toward Birchmount Rd, so drivers swerve into the next lane to avoid it.

Two neighbours have already reported rim and suspension damage after hitting it at night, when standing water hides how deep it is. The patch applied in the spring washed out after the first heavy rain.
Requesting a permanent resurfacing of the section rather than another cold patch, plus temporary cones until the crew can be scheduled.

updates.title: Report submitted
updates.note: Issue received with photo and video evidence and queued for triage.

updates.title: Verified by field inspector
updates.note: Location and severity confirmed on site. Logged as a road hazard and routed to Transportation Services.

updates.title: Repair crew scheduled
updates.note: Cones placed around the hazard. Hot-mix resurfacing booked for the next dry weather window.

posts.title: Flooding during heavy rain
posts.desc: Water is not draining properly on this street after rain.
posts.address: 880 Morningside Ave, between Coronation Dr and Beechgrove
details: After any rainfall over about 20 minutes, water pools from the driveway at 880 Morningside Ave all the way across both lanes. The pool reaches the middle of a car tire and takes close to three hours to drain once the rain stops.
The catch basin at the corner looks completely blocked — leaves and silt sit level with the grate, and no water moves through it even when the street is flooded.
Pedestrians have to walk on the road to get around the water because the sidewalk dips lower than the curb here. This is the fourth time this season.

updates.title: Report submitted
updates.note: Flooding reported with photos taken during the Oct 25 rainfall.

updates.title: Awaiting inspection
updates.note: Flagged as critical because of standing water on an active roadway. Catch basin inspection requested.

posts.title: Broken sidewalk near bus stop
posts.desc: The sidewalk is cracked and unsafe for pedestrians.
posts.address: 2301 Sheppard Ave W, at the westbound bus stop
details: Three concrete slabs beside the westbound bus stop have lifted and cracked, leaving a step of about 4 cm between them right where passengers board.
Two regular riders at this stop use walkers, and one caught a wheel on the raised edge last week. The gap also traps water that freezes overnight.
The slabs were ground down and relaid, and the surface is now level with the boarding pad.

updates.title: Report submitted
updates.note: Trip hazard reported next to a transit boarding area.

updates.title: Work order issued
updates.note: Concrete crew assigned; temporary asphalt wedge installed the same afternoon.

updates.title: Repair completed
updates.note: Slabs replaced and the walkway levelled to the boarding pad. Photo proof added to the file.

posts.title: Streetlight not working
posts.desc: This streetlight has been out for over a week.
posts.address: 1455 Markham Rd, opposite the pharmacy entrance
details: The pole-mounted light outside 1455 Markham Rd has been dark for nine nights. The two poles on either side work, so the gap leaves the crosswalk and the pharmacy entrance in shadow.
The stretch is busy after 7pm with people walking to the bus loop, and several have said they now cross at the next intersection instead.
The pole number on the plate is MK-4471 if that helps the crew locate it.

updates.title: Report submitted
updates.note: Outage reported for pole MK-4471.

updates.title: Diagnosed as ballast failure
updates.note: Crew tested the circuit and confirmed a failed ballast. Replacement part ordered.

posts.title: Recycling bins uncollected for two weeks
posts.desc: Blue bins have been left full on the curb since the last two pickup days.
posts.address: 3150 Kingston Rd, east side of the block
details: Blue bins for the whole east side of the block have been skipped on the last two collection days. Residents left them out both Tuesdays and the truck passed without stopping.
Overflow is now stacked beside the bins in bags, and wind has scattered cardboard and plastic along the sidewalk and into the ravine path at the end of the street.
Garbage and organics are still being collected normally on the same route, so it appears to be the recycling run specifically.

updates.title: Report submitted
updates.note: Missed recycling collection reported for a full block.

updates.title: Route audit opened
updates.note: Collection logs pulled for the Tuesday run. A catch-up truck is being scheduled for this block.

posts.title: Damaged playground swing set
posts.desc: A swing chain has snapped and the seat is hanging loose at the north playground.
details: One of the four swings at the north playground has a snapped chain on the left side, so the seat hangs at an angle about a foot off the ground.
Small children keep climbing onto it because nothing marks it as broken, and the loose chain end is at head height for a toddler.
The swing was taken out of service the same day and a new chain and seat were fitted two days later.

updates.title: Report submitted
updates.note: Broken swing reported with a photo of the snapped chain.

updates.title: Equipment taken out of service
updates.note: Swing removed and the frame taped off pending replacement parts.

updates.title: Swing replaced
updates.note: New chain and seat installed, and the full set was inspected for wear.

posts.title: Water main leak flooding the curb lane
posts.desc: Clean water has been running from under the pavement for three days straight.
posts.address: 2740 Ellesmere Rd, west of Neilson Rd
details: Clear water has been running continuously from a crack in the curb lane for three days, even with no rain. The flow is steady enough to keep a channel of water along the gutter for most of the block.
The asphalt around the crack is beginning to sink, and there is a soft spot roughly a metre wide that moves under a car tire.
Two houses on this stretch reported lower water pressure starting the same morning the leak appeared.

updates.title: Report submitted
updates.note: Continuous water flow reported with a note about reduced pressure nearby.

updates.title: Leak confirmed and lane closed
updates.note: Acoustic survey located a break on the 150 mm main. Curb lane closed and excavation permit filed.

updates.title: Repair crew mobilised
updates.note: Excavation underway. A short shutoff is planned for the block during the repair.

posts.title: Bus shelter glass smashed at the eastbound stop
posts.desc: The side panel is shattered and glass fragments are spread across the pad.
details: The rear panel of the eastbound shelter is shattered, with most of the glass still held in the frame and a spread of fragments across the concrete pad and the grass behind it.
With the panel gone the bench offers no protection from wind or rain, and riders have been standing out at the curb instead of using the shelter.
The pad was swept and a replacement panel was fitted the following week.

updates.title: Report submitted
updates.note: Vandalised shelter panel reported with broken glass on the boarding pad.

updates.title: Glass cleared from the site
updates.note: Fragments swept and the frame taped pending a replacement panel.

updates.title: Panel replaced
updates.note: New tempered glass panel installed and the shelter returned to service.

postComments.author: Derek Mensah
postComments.body: Hit this on Saturday night and bent a rim. There is no warning at all once it rains and the hole fills up. Thanks for filing it with the video, that shows the depth much better than a photo.

replies.author: Amina R.
replies.body: Sorry to hear that. Keep the repair invoice — the claims desk asked me for mine when I reported the damage last month.

postComments.author: Eng. Daniel Okafor
postComments.body: Transportation Services has this one. Cones are up as of this afternoon and the section is booked for hot-mix resurfacing in the next dry window rather than another cold patch. I will post here once the crew is on site.

postComments.author: Shelly Vance
postComments.body: Our delivery vans use this lane every morning. Could the crew also look at the smaller cracks about ten metres east? They are heading the same way this one did.

replies.author: Insp. Laila Haque
replies.body: Noted during the site visit. The whole stretch between the driveway and the bus pad is in the same work order, so those cracks are covered.

postComments.author: Owen Brar
postComments.body: Cyclists are swerving into the live lane to get around it, which feels more dangerous than the hole itself. Glad this is moving.

postComments.author: Councillor Mira Ahmed
postComments.body: My office is tracking this alongside two similar reports on Finch. If the resurfacing slips past this week, email us and we will push for an interim barrier.

postComments.author: Helena Cruz
postComments.body: Same every storm. I measured it on Sunday and the water sat about 15 cm deep at the low point, right where people step off the sidewalk.

replies.author: Marcus D.
replies.body: That matches what I saw. If you have photos from Sunday, adding them here would help — the more dates on file, the harder it is to call this a one-off.

postComments.author: Raj Patel
postComments.body: Customers cannot reach our entrance for a couple of hours after every heavy rain. We have swept the grate ourselves twice, but it clogs again almost immediately.

postComments.author: Intake Desk
postComments.body: Logged as critical because of standing water on an active roadway. A catch basin inspection has been requested; the crew will confirm whether the blockage is at the grate or further down the lateral.

postComments.author: Nina Sorensen
postComments.body: Worth checking the basin across the street too. It drains fine, which makes me think the problem is specific to the one on this corner.

postComments.author: Albert Fung
postComments.body: I catch the 84 here every morning and the lifted slab was easy to miss in the dark. The new surface is level now — much better for anyone boarding with a walker.

replies.author: Supt. Priya Menon
replies.body: Thanks for confirming. The slabs were relaid level with the boarding pad and photo proof is attached to the file. Flag it here if any settling shows up over the winter.

postComments.author: Grace T.
postComments.body: Quick turnaround on this one — reported Saturday morning and the temporary wedge was in by the afternoon. Thank you to the crew.

postComments.author: Lydia Novak
postComments.body: Could the same crew look at the stretch two stops east? The cracking pattern there looks like the early stage of this.

postComments.author: Jordan Ellis
postComments.body: Walk past here most evenings and the gap between the two working poles is very dark. I have started crossing at the next intersection instead.

postComments.author: Tech. Omar Siddiqui
postComments.body: Circuit tested at pole MK-4471 and the ballast has failed. The replacement part is ordered; once it arrives the swap takes under an hour.

postComments.author: Fatima Noor
postComments.body: Our pharmacy closes at nine and staff have asked to be walked to their cars because of this. Appreciate the pole number being in the report.

postComments.author: Beatrice Lam
postComments.body: Collection logs for the Tuesday run are being audited. A catch-up truck is being scheduled for this block, and the overflow bags will be taken at the same time.

postComments.author: Henry Okonjo
postComments.body: Garbage and organics were both picked up on schedule, so it is only the recycling run skipping us. Third time this year on this block.

replies.author: Samuel O.
replies.body: Same on my side. I have been photographing the bins each collection morning so there is a record of the dates.

postComments.author: Priya S.
postComments.body: The new chain and seat are in and the rest of the set was checked at the same time. Two days from report to repair on a playground is a good result.

postComments.author: Ranger Ellis Moreau
postComments.body: Swing is back in service. If anything on this structure starts to rattle or sag, report it right away rather than waiting — chain wear tends to show up gradually.

postComments.author: Tomas V.
postComments.body: Flow has not stopped since Tuesday and the soft spot in the asphalt is now wide enough that you can feel it through the steering wheel.

replies.author: Eng. Hannah Whitfield
replies.body: The acoustic survey put the break on the 150 mm main under that soft spot, which is why the surface is sinking. Excavation is underway and there will be a short shutoff for the block during the repair.

postComments.author: Margaret Ibe
postComments.body: Our pressure dropped the same morning the water appeared at the curb, so the two are almost certainly the same break.

postComments.author: Victor Lau
postComments.body: Please post the shutoff window here when it is set. We run a cafe on this block and need an hour of notice to fill containers.

postComments.author: Councillor Mira Ahmed
postComments.body: Shutoff notices will be dropped at every address on the block and posted on this thread the day before. Businesses needing a longer window can contact my office.

postComments.author: Wei L.
postComments.body: Panel is replaced and the pad was swept clean. Riders are using the shelter again instead of standing out at the curb.

postComments.author: Coord. Felix Nunez
postComments.body: Tempered glass is in and the shelter is back in service. Reports of broken glass at transit stops are cleared the same day even when the panel takes longer to arrive.
